web_evidence.title: Bag of Bones | Book by Stephen King | Official Publisher Page
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained Chapter 1 excerpt is narrated by Mike Noonan as I and my, beginning with his account of his wife's death.

web_evidence.title: Bag of Bones Reading Group Guide and Extract
web_evidence.note: The authorized UK publisher guide supplies a sustained later extract in which Mike narrates his dreams of Sara Laughs through I and my.

web_evidence.title: The Haunted House of Memory in the Fiction of Stephen King
web_evidence.note: Will Napier's University of Glasgow PhD thesis explicitly states that Bag of Bones is told through a first-person narrator and identifies that narrator as Mike Noonan.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King Writing Styles in Bag of Bones
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view section explicitly describes the novel as entirely first person through protagonist Mike Noonan.

web_evidence.title: Books: Don't mention the king
web_evidence.note: Kim Newman's review identifies Michael Noonan as the narrator and describes the completed narrative as Noonan's memoir, including its final chapter.

web_evidence.title: Bag of Bones by Stephen King
web_evidence.note: The contemporary review identifies Mike Noonan as the narrator and attributes the novel's opening account and continuing broodings to him.

search_log: Searched: Stephen King Bag of Bones excerpt first chapter publisher; opened the Simon & Schuster official book page and its Chapter 1 excerpt.
Searched: Bag of Bones Stephen King first person narrator point of view; opened explicit point-of-view descriptions from BookRags and contemporary reviews.
Searched: Bag of Bones novel narration first person Mike Noonan scholarly; opened two academic theses, including the University of Glasgow PhD close reading.
Searched: site:stephenking.com Bag of Bones excerpt; no useful extract appeared on the author site, but the search located an authorized Stephen King UK publisher guide with an extract.
Searched targeted combinations for multiple narrators, alternating point of view, epistolary form, and frame narrative; found no credible indication of sustained base sections in another person.
Opened Publishers Weekly, The Independent, Salon, and the authorized excerpts to distinguish explicit narrator evidence from synopsis grammar.

An AudioFile result explicitly described the audiobook as a first-person narrative in its search result, but the live page redirected to a generic audiobook index, so it was not retained as web evidence.
Hachette UK's product page advertised an excerpt but exposed only catalog copy in the accessible page; it was treated as a discovery dead end.
person_note: The diagnostic event quotes repeatedly expose bestselling novelist Mike Noonan as a participating I-narrator, including sustained autobiographical passages about his wife, grief, writer's block, and later experiences. Third-person scenic sentences are merely unmarked within that first-person account, while dialogue and gnomic quotations were not promoted to base-narrator evidence; q00211 and q00228 remain locally unresolved because context was stripped. Independent authorized opening and interior extracts reproduce Mike's first-person voice, and scholarly whole-book analysis explicitly identifies the novel's first-person narrator. Targeted searches found no sustained second- or third-person base sections, so the controlling narrative person is FIRST with no material remaining structural uncertainty.
